sentences.text: Wellbore 15/9-F-1 C (Sodir wellbore 7405, Volve, purpose production, status P&A) has drilling reports from 2014-02-21 to 2016-10-21.
The report span is 973.96 d with 98 active days, split into 5 campaigns.
The deepest measured depth reported is 4094.0 m with a true vertical depth of 3180.5 m, and Sodir gives the same total depth of 4094.0 m.
Total activity time is 2220.25 h, of which primary lost time is 329.0 h, a share of 14.82 % of the activity time.
Sodir gives an entry date of 2014-02-21 and a completion date of 2014-03-18, which is the end of drilling and not production start-up.

The reports run far beyond that date because the well was drilled to total depth in three hole sections, then completed, worked over and finally plugged and abandoned; section 5, the first completion section, starts on 2014-03-18.

The main outcome is a well drilled to total depth, completed and perforated, later produced and then plugged and abandoned; the heaviest lost time came from waiting on weather, rig and crane repairs, and completion-phase equipment problems.
Campaign 1 runs from 2014-02-21 to 2014-04-21, spans 59.96 d with 60 active days, and its dominant operation phase is completion (it includes the three drilling sections).
Campaign 2 runs from 2014-11-27 to 2014-12-06, spans 10.0 d with 10 active days, and is a workover.
Campaign 3 runs from 2016-06-15 to 2016-07-08, spans 24.0 d with 24 active days, and is plug and abandon.
Campaign 4 runs from 2016-09-16 to 2016-09-18, spans 3.0 d with 3 active days, and is plug and abandon.
Campaign 5 is a single plug and abandon day on 2016-10-21, spanning 1.0 d with 1 active day.
Section 1 is a 17.5 in hole drilled from 2014-02-21 to 2014-03-02, from 1364.0 m to 2514.0 m measured depth, with a true vertical depth of 2451.9 m at section end and 1150.0 m of new hole.
The average rate while coded drilling -- drill (not an on-bottom rate of penetration) was 22.01 m/h in section 1.
Section 2 is a 12.25 in hole drilled from 2014-03-03 to 2014-03-10, from 2517.0 m to 3059.0 m measured depth, with a true vertical depth of 2874.4 m at section end and 545.0 m of new hole.
The average rate while coded drilling -- drill (not an on-bottom rate of penetration) was 13.97 m/h in section 2.
Section 3 is an 8.5 in hole drilled from 2014-03-11 to 2014-03-14, from 3059.0 m to 4094.0 m measured depth, with a true vertical depth of 3180.5 m at section end and 1035.0 m of new hole.
The average rate while coded drilling -- drill (not an on-bottom rate of penetration) was 19.26 m/h in section 3.

Sections 4 to 14 have an unknown hole size (hole_size_source is unknown), drilled no new hole and have no time coded drilling -- drill, so no drilling rate exists for them; they are the end-of-drilling, completion, workover and plug and abandon sections.
For sections 4 to 12 and section 14 the tools give the section end true vertical depth as the same total-depth value; section 13 (workover) reports no end measured depth or true vertical depth.
Section 1 starts below a casing shoe at 1348.4 m and sets casing with its shoe at 2507.7 m.
Section 2 starts below the shoe at 2507.7 m and sets casing with its shoe at 3047.0 m.
Section 3 starts below the shoe at 3047.0 m and no casing shoe is recorded for the section (casing shoe not reported).
From section 5 onward the deepest shoe at section start is 4087.1 m, and no casing is recorded as set in sections 4 to 14 by the tools.

sentences.text: The tools give no casing size; the only report text I cite that names one is the activity comment on 2014-02-23, which records preparing casing during a weather wait in section 1: "M/U 13 3/8" casing and R/B 4 stands in derrick".
Primary lost time by section: section 1 lost 72.25 h (32.04 % of the section's activity time), section 2 lost 9.75 h (5.08 %), and section 3 lost 19.25 h (20.05 %).
In the completion and later sections, section 6 lost 81.0 h (48.21 %), section 7 lost 50.5 h (52.6 %), and section 14 (plug and abandon) lost 90.75 h (14.73 %).
The smaller primary amounts are 0.75 h in section 4, 2.0 h in section 9 and 2.75 h in section 13; sections 5, 8, 10, 11 and 12 have no primary lost time.

By cause, primary lost time is 186.0 h coded interruption -- repair, 120.5 h coded interruption -- waiting on weather, 18.25 h coded interruption -- wait and 4.25 h coded interruption -- fish, together 329.0 h or 14.82 % of the wellbore activity time.

Possible lost time is reported separately and is not added to the primary figures: it totals 81.25 h or 3.66 % of the activity time, of which 79.75 h is coded interruption -- other and 1.5 h interruption -- maintain.
Waiting on weather, with cuttings that could not be discharged to a vessel, interrupted the 17.5 in section from 2014-02-22, and the wait was still recorded on 2014-02-26 for 4.25 h.

On 2014-03-11 the crew decided to pull out of hole and change the AutoTrak rotary steerable system after diagnostics, a 2.25 h entry coded possible lost time; the trip and tool change that followed were coded primary repair time in section 3.
From 2014-03-22 the rig waited on a weather window to disconnect and pull the high-pressure drilling riser, 33.25 h in total over four entries.
From 2014-03-25 the rig waited on repair of the port crane brake system, 27.75 h across three entries coded primary repair time.
On 2014-04-02 the adjustable setting tool for the tie-back adapter could not be pulled free and was recovered with a broken locking ring after 5.0 h of attempts, evaluation and annular-pressure work.
During perforating, the tractor failed and the toolstring stopped moving in the deviated hole on 2014-04-13 (2.0 h) and again on 2014-04-15 (2.25 h); these entries are coded possible lost time.
On 2016-06-29 the string stuck while working the work string during plug and abandon and could not be freed, a 5.25 h entry coded primary repair time.
Waiting for the wireline cutting equipment to be mobilised then started on 2016-06-29 and took 24.0 h across five entries, after which the string was cut on 2016-07-01.

Plan weather and logistics margins for the first section and for riser work, because waiting on weather accounts for most of the primary lost time in section 1 and a large block in section 6, so the next well should schedule marine-critical jobs (cuttings transfer, riser handling) in weather windows and keep spare iso-tank capacity.

Verify the rotary steerable system and gyro before running them, because the steerable tool change and gyro communication problems in sections 2 and 3 added trips coded as primary repair and possible lost time.

Qualify tie-back and setting tools and the rig crane before the completion campaign, because the broken setting-tool locking ring and the crane brake failure drove the high primary lost-time shares in sections 6 and 7.

Check the perforating tractor against the deviation of the well before the run, because the toolstring stopped in the deviated hole on two runs and tractor wheels were missing after one of them; these hours are possible, not primary, lost time.

For plug and abandon, have the wireline cutting equipment and personnel on the rig before pulling the completion, because a stuck string followed by a long wait for the cutter, together with repeated pipe-handling repairs, produced the largest section primary lost time in section 14.

row.comments: Waited one weather, not able to discharge cuttings to vessel due to bad weather.                           Circulated btm's up due to full iso tanks with 4000 lpm, 235 bar, 130-140 rpm, 3-6 kNm. ECD 1,43 SG. Max gas 0,02 %. Reciprocated pipe.

WOW.
M/U 13 3/8" casing and R/B 4 stands in derrick. M/U shoe track, backer locked and tested floats with water.

Waited one weather from 00:45 to 04:15 hrs. 
Not able to discharge cuttings to vessel due to bad weather.
Circulated well clean with with 4200 lpm, 265 bar, 130 rpm, 4-6 kNm. ECD 1,44 SG. Max gas 0,02 %.

Established circulation and sent downlink. RIH to bottom and circulated with 2200 l/min. Baker performed diagnostics on downhole tools. Pulled into 9 5/8" shoe and continued troubleshooting on AutoTrak RSS.
Decided to POOH and change AutoTrak RSS.

Waited on Weather window (12 hrs) for disconnecting and pulling HPDR.
Meanwhile performed maintenance and started to change out wire on aft PRS.

Waited on Weather window (12 hrs) for disconnecting and pulling HPDR.
Meanwhile performed maintenance jobs and continued to change out wire on aft PRS.
Installed 2 guidewires.

Waited on Weather window (12 hrs) for disconnecting and pulling HPDR.
Meanwhile performed maintenance jobs and pressure tested BOP and manifolds to 20/345bar 5/10min. Spotted Well Partner equipment on rig floor.

Waited on Weather window (12 hrs) for disconnecting and pulling HPDR.
Meanwhile performed maintenance jobs and pressure tested manifolds to 20/345bar 5/10min.
Rigged up hot stab sheaves in moonpool.
Advised Production to shut down at 05:43 hrs.

Waited on Crane repair: Trouble shot problem with fluctating pressure on Port Crane emergency brake.
Started to change out pump.

Hoisted Tension joint above RKB. Closed spider and secured C-plates on top. Informed Production to start up at 13:00 hrs.

Meanwhile pressure tested TDS auto/man IBOP and Kelly hose to 20/345 bar for 5/10 min.
M/U RT for Production Riser to std and racked in derrick. Performed maintenance and derrick inspection.

Continued changing out pump on Port crane. Further cleaned oil system and changed oil.
Meanwhile ROV cleaned and installed VX gasket and Debris cap.
Continued to perform maintenance on drilling equipment.

Waited on crane repair.
Meanwhile performed maintenance including 5 yearly on choke manifold valve C7.
Assisted on crane repair.
Attempted several times to POOH with adjustable setting tool with no success.
Brainstorm. Discussed problem with town.
Closed annular, applied 20 bar on annulus. Pulled tool free and up 2 m with no over pull.
Opened annular and released pressure while pulled up 3 m with 6-8 ton drag. Observed 15 ton over pull, slacked of weight.
Closed annular, applied 20 bar on annulus. Stripped out to 19 m with 3 ton over pull. Bleed off pressure and opened annular.
POOH with adjustable setting tool from 19 m to surface. Inspected tool and observed locking ring broken in 3 pieces.

RIH with perforation string no 6. on WL with 30 m/min to 3250 m. Re-run.
Correlated across DHPG @ 2640 m. 
Toolstring stopped moving at 3250 m / 78 deg inclination.

RIH with perforation string no 7. on WL with 30 m/min to 3261 m. Re-run.
Toolstring stopped moving at 3261 m / 79 deg inclination.

Observed overpull when picking up work string between 138t and 300t on martin decker. String stuck @ 2362m.  Tried to work string free. Max pulled to 320t, max torque 40knm, sat down all string weight. No success to get string free. Evaluated further steps, started mobilizing WL cutter equipment to cut inside DP.
Waited for WL cutting equipment and personnel to be mobilized. Meanwhile worked on repairing forward PRS
Waited for WL cutting equipment and personnel to be mobilized. Meanwhile worked on repairing forward PRS. Greased manifolds
Waited for WL cutting equipment and personnel to be mobilized. Meanwhile test run forward PRS
Waited for WL cutting equipment to be mobilized. Meanwhile worked on repairing forward PRS. L/O stand of 7in tbg

Waited for WL cutting equipment to be mobilized. Meanwhile worked on repairing forward PRS, trouble shoot PRS setdown load indication. Prepared for WL work. Changed out PS21 to master bushings, cleared rig floor.
Waited for WL cutting equipment to be mobilized. Meanwhile L/O 7in tbg stand from derrick. Rig down csg tong equipment, prepared to break out and changed spear assembly
Applied 10 Ton overpull to drill string, 153T on Martin Decker. Set WL anchor. Cut csg. Took 7 min to make cut
